title: Forces as interactions with agent and receiver

authority_basis.claim_scope: Every force is an interaction exerted by an agent on a receiver.

concepts.statement: Every force in a Newtonian model is exerted by an identified agent on an identified receiver.
concepts.why_required: Force is an interaction relation, not a substance or intrinsic property carried by an object.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Free-body diagrams can contain unnamed or physically impossible forces with no identified agent.

model_conditions.condition: A receiver body or system boundary is selected before interactions are classified.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Whether an interaction is external or internal depends on the chosen system boundary.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Forces can be assigned to the wrong receiver or internal interactions can be mistaken for external forces.

representations.semantic_geometry: Nodes represent physical bodies or systems and labelled links represent contact or non-contact interactions between an agent and receiver.
must_not_imply: a force exists without an interacting agent
an interaction link is itself a free-body force arrow
representations.verification_method: For every candidate force, name the external agent and receiver and check that the interaction crosses the selected system boundary.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Choose the receiver body or system before naming forces.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The force list has no stable system boundary.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: List physical contact and non-contact interactions crossing the selected system boundary.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A real interaction can be omitted or an internal interaction can be included incorrectly.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Name each force explicitly as force by agent on receiver.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Later third-law and free-body reasoning cannot distinguish force pairs reliably.

required_transformations.description: Convert a physical scene into explicit agent-receiver interaction links before drawing force arrows.
Use each external interaction to justify a corresponding force candidate on the selected receiver.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: An object contains or carries force as an intrinsic property.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Everyday phrases such as 'the object has force' obscure the interaction partner and receiver.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A freely moving object can continue with constant velocity after the pushing interaction ends; it does not carry the push force with it.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Replace isolated force labels with an interaction map that names both bodies in each interaction.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Name the external agent that exerts each force on the chosen receiver.
misconceptions.verification: Every force arrow must answer 'force by what on what?' with a physical interaction.

problem_families.name: Identify external forces on a selected system
recognition_cues: object in contact with surfaces or strings
problem_families.first_technical_move: Select the receiver and list interactions crossing its boundary.
fatal_errors: inventing motion-direction force with no agent

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove agent-receiver interaction identity from the Newtonian interaction gate.
